source.title: Semantic Structure in Large Language Model Embeddings
source.authors: Austin C. Kozlowski; Callin Dai; Andrei Boutyline

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses superposition and reports new results about semantic feature directions in LLM embedding matrices, but does not test the versions as stated: it does not test sparse overcomplete toy networks, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAE features, or whether the model's actual features are one- rather than multi-dimensional.
record.gate_note: The reported semantic-direction geometry and steering results are relevant adjacent findings, recorded under fits_no_version. They do not establish that sparse features are superposed because there are more features than dimensions. The paper's background discussion of superposition is not itself a result. Results attributed to cited prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper builds antonym-difference directions in LLM input embedding matrices and measures their alignment, PCA structure and steering off-target effects. Its superposition discussion (Section 2.2) is background and argument. There is no toy network with sparse features outnumbering dimensions, and no neuron-level polysemanticity, capacity, SAE or multi-dimensional-feature test. Its claim that alignment is semantic 'not out of an accident of superposition' concerns constructed semantic axes, not any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. It should add that the authors argue feature non-orthogonality in embeddings reflects natural semantic correlation, 'not out of an accident of superposition'. They also argue whitening-style orthogonalisation distorts concepts, and that low-dimensional semantic structure may simplify auditing and control.
record.recipe_differences: Uses antonym-pair mean directions in LLM input embedding matrices, token projections, PCA, and embedding interventions; it does not reproduce the original toy-network setup or its sparsity/feature-count sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Whitening reduced average token-level correspondence with survey ratings by approximately 20%; reported semantic-feature relationships vary by model family and size, with the authors noting moderately weaker relationships for Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 than Gemma-3.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-3-12B, cosine similarities among 28 antonym-defined embedding directions are often 0.1–0.3 and correlate 0.76 with human survey scale correlations. Projection correlation matrices match the survey at r=0.82 (survey words) and r=0.73 (full vocabulary).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-orthogonality among semantic directions in LLM input embeddings is structured and mirrors human semantic correlations, not random interference.

fits_no_version.finding: Three principal components retain 40–55% of variance across 28 semantic projections in Gemma-3 embeddings. The loadings resemble Evaluation/Activity-like factors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Semantic projections in LLM embeddings are partly low-dimensional.

fits_no_version.finding: Whitening embeddings lowers the average correspondence with human ratings by about 20%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decorrelating embedding directions reduces fidelity to human semantic associations.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering a token embedding along one semantic direction causes off-target effects scaling with cosine similarity: about 10 pp for the most aligned pairs in Gemma-3-1B, and smaller but clear effects in 12B and 27B (p<0.001).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric alignment of semantic directions predicts off-target steering effects.

record.problems: The findings use semantic directions defined from antonym pairs in input embedding matrices and do not establish that these are the models' complete or canonical features. The main text gives limited separate numerical detail for model-specific geometry and off-target effects; several plotted results are not numerically tabulated in the text. The study does not test sparse overcomplete storage, toy-network transitions, neuron-level polysemanticity, or SAE recovery.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 7–15 show additional model-family results, including Llama and Qwen correlations, PCA, and off-target effects, but the text provides no separately described numerical values for these results; they are not added as separate rows. Cited findings from other studies are omitted.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or toy geometry.
No capacity pressure or dedicated-vs-shared dimension test; neurons are not analysed.
No measurement of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
No measurement of features distributed across neurons and no SAE recovery. Directions are constructed from antonym pairs.
1-D directions are assumed by construction; feature dimensionality is not tested.

missing.what: Per-feature correlations between projections and human ratings range from 0.3 to 0.7; no row records this validation.
Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 results (up to 72B), described as similar patterns with moderately weaker relationships.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's gate is correct. The paper contests framing off-target effects as random superposition, but this concerns constructed antonym directions in input embeddings, not any listed version, so it gives no verdicts. It is a preprint; no code release is stated.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; no sparsity sweep, transition, or regular toy-model geometry test.
No test of capacity pressure, dedicated versus shared dimensions, or neuron polysemanticity.
No test of non-capacity mechanisms producing polysemantic neurons.
Does not measure features spread across neurons or features recovered by an SAE; it studies semantic directions in the input embedding matrix.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical.

Uses one-dimensional semantic direction vectors as its analysis method, but does not test whether the model's represented or superposed features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.measure: Pearson correlation between feature-vector cosine similarities and corresponding survey correlation coefficients
rows.note: This measures alignment among the paper's constructed semantic directions, not overcomplete feature storage.

rows.subject: Gemma-3-12B
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise cosine similarities between 28 semantic feature vectors.
rows.measure: Pairwise cosine similarity of semantic feature vectors
rows.value: Many similarities are less than 0.05; many are between 0.1 and 0.3.
rows.note: The result concerns semantic axes constructed from antonym-pair differences.

rows.subject: Gemma-3 models
rows.operation_detail: Applied PCA to projections of 301 word vectors on 28 semantic feature vectors.
rows.measure: Variance preserved by a three-dimensional PCA solution
rows.value: Between 40 and 55% of variance across 28 original features.
rows.note: The text gives a range across LLM embeddings rather than separate values for each Gemma size. The paper describes the resulting structure as low-dimensional and similar, but not identical, to survey structure.
rows.check: The 40–55% range is given across LLM embeddings, not per Gemma size. Per-model values appear only in Figure 5.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared token-level semantic projections with human survey ratings before and after whitening the embedding space.
rows.measure: Average token-level correlation with corresponding survey ratings
rows.baseline: Unwhitened embeddings; exact value not stated.
rows.value: Whitening reduced the average correlation by approximately 20%.
rows.note: The paper states the reduction but does not identify the model for this result in the accompanying text.
rows.check: This compares the study's projection method against the Park et al. whitened alternative, so it is a method comparison. 'partial' has no version referent. The model is not named in the text (Figure 3; the main analyses are on Gemma-3). The unwhitened baseline value is not stated.

rows.subject: Gemma-3-1B
rows.operation_detail: Related off-target changes in reported semantic associations to cosine similarity between target and off-target feature vectors after token-embedding interventions.

conditions.value: move target token embedding along a semantic feature direction; scaled to ±0.35 of token-vector norm and renormalized

rows.measure: Off-target effect size as a function of target/off-target feature-vector cosine similarity
rows.baseline: Baseline next-token probabilities collected before intervention; exact values not stated.
rows.value: The strongest effects occur in the smallest model; the most aligned feature pairs exhibit average off-target effects of 10 percentage points.
rows.note: This is an off-target steering result for the study's semantic directions, not evidence of sparse-feature superposition.
